subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which default policy and implementation sequence should OpenClaw use to reduce model-facing tool-schema overhead without breaking cross-channel cron/isolated agents, provider schema contracts, or plugin/declarative tools?
rationale: The remaining work changes default prompt/schema visibility and crosses provider payloads, channel compatibility, Tool Search/deferred-schema semantics, plugin APIs, and possible config knobs, so maintainer intent is needed before implementation.

options.title: Sequence narrow reductions
options.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred/slim schema design.

options.title: Defer to narrower issues
options.body: Close the umbrella and require all remaining work to happen only through linked focused issues such as prompt-text skipping or deferred tool registration.

options.title: Adopt aggressive lazy defaults
options.body: Make lazy or slim schemas the default now, accepting a broader compatibility and provider-contract review burden up front.

recommendation.title: Sequence narrow reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred/slim schema design.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest source history and issue discussion point to steipete as the best available routing owner for prompt/runtime schema sequencing.
